audit_notes: Geometry: s = 80 um (s+ = 14.8), riblet height not given; assumed h = 0.5 s = 40 um (h+ = 7.4). Wavelength 1.5 mm -> lambda_x+ = 278, amplitude 100 um -> A+ = 18.5, crest slope 2 pi A/lambda = 0.42. The induced spanwise velocity at the riblet tips is W ~ u(y+~7)*slope -> W+ ~ 3, confined to y+ < ~10. Stationary spanwise-wave forcing is most effective at lambda_x+ ~ 1000-1250 with W+ ~ 12 and a Stokes layer penetrating to y+ ~ 10-20 (Quadrio et al. 2009); here both wavelength and amplitude are below optimum, so only a small increment over straight riblets can be expected, and experiments on sinusoidal riblets (Grueneberger et al. 2012; Kramer et al. 2010) show gains between -1 and +2 percentage points depending on setup. The increased effective spanwise exposure of meandering crests also raises h_perp. I therefore reduce effective_protrusion_difference from 5.5 um to 4.5 um (same as well-designed straight riblets, 0.056 s): expected gain 4.5/99.5 = 4.5%. Structural: silicone crests unchanged vs straight riblets; meandering improves crest robustness slightly (lateral support), but grooves still foul. Pipeline riblet formula not applicable here (no riblet_height parameter); simulation coefficient = protrusion difference.
